A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Toward Understanding In-Context vs. In-Weight Learning. The main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite appendix reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic classification, Omniglot and Gemini Nano 1 experiments in Sections 3–4, with additional results in Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including empirical learning curves and base-versus-finetuned Gemini predictions and log-probabilities.

M1.justification: The gated combination of IW and IC predictors and Algorithm 1's updates are unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds analysis of the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Synthetic classification, Omniglot and Gemini name–city tasks retain the same coverage, including shifted-label evaluation, heldout images and conflicting-context prompts.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same IW/IC predictors, transformer, stylized-model and GRU comparisons, and base-versus-finetuned Gemini comparison. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–D retain the same sampling procedures, training budgets, model configurations, IBD/OOBD evaluation, metrics and prompt procedures.

E4.justification: Noise, class-frequency, class-cardinality, context-length and context-relevance analyses are retained, as are attention visualizations, heldout-image tests and extended-training experiments. Apparent appendix differences reflect relocated text.

E5.justification: The five-seed synthetic experiments, three-seed Omniglot experiments and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The empirical curves and findings, including appendix results, are unchanged. Tables 2–3 retain identical Gemini predictions and log-probabilities; the added proposition supplies no new empirical results.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 introduces Proposition 5 and its proof. Alongside Proposition 2's comparison against the best IW predictor, it states a bound against a best-in-hindsight combined predictor, involving gating regret and separate IW/IC regrets over a hindsight partition. This substantially broadens the formal comparison being claimed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: explaining ICL emergence and transience through competition with IWL, supported by synthetic, Omniglot and language-model experiments.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 adds the interpretation that Algorithm 1 converges to the best-in-hindsight predictor generally, extending its preceding discussion of the best IW predictor. Empirical interpretations and the unresolved transience cases discussed in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository link at the beginning of Appendix B; v2 provides no such pointer. Implementation details and experimental hyperparameters otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, reference list and positioning relative to previous ICL/IWL research are unchanged. The new theoretical subsection adds no cited research.

P1.justification: v3 adds subsection A.2 and a short cross-reference in Section 2.3. Existing wording and the overall narrative structure are otherwise retained, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The long display in Proposition 2's proof is split across additional lines, and appendix text and figures reflow, including the discussion accompanying Figures 19–20. Figure content, captions and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The code pointer and clearer equation layout are useful, but the main addition has unresolved scope issues. Proposition 5 assumes a binary hindsight-optimal gate although Section 2.1 permits continuous mixtures, and does not establish sublinear regret on the selected IW/IC subsequences. Consequently, Section 2.3's new general-convergence statement is not fully justified by the added derivation, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
